answer: Four large outcome trials define the field: Lp(a)HORIZON with pelacarsen, negative in September 2026; OCEAN(a)-Outcomes with olpasiran, about 7,300 people, expected late 2026 or 2027; ACCLAIM-Lp(a) with lepodisiran, about 17,300 people, around 2029; and MOVE-Lp(a) with muvalaplin, around 2031.

sections.body: If your Lp(a) is high, ask your cardiologist whether you could join one of these trials.
sections.heading: What it means for patients

explainer:
Outcome trials compare a drug with placebo on top of standard care and count events such as cardiovascular death, heart attack, stroke and urgent revascularisation. They need thousands of participants and several years because events are uncommon.

Differences between trials matter for interpreting results: the Lp(a) threshold for entry, whether participants already have heart disease, how deeply the drug lowers Lp(a), how long they are followed, and how well other risk factors are already controlled. Lp(a)HORIZON enrolled people on optimised background therapy, which may have left less room to show benefit.

developments.text: Lp(a)HORIZON (NCT04023552), 8,323 patients, did not meet its primary endpoint.
OCEAN(a)-Outcomes tests olpasiran in people with atherosclerotic disease and Lp(a) of at least 200 nmol/L.
ACCLAIM-Lp(a) tests lepodisiran in people with atherosclerotic disease or at high risk with Lp(a) of at least 175 nmol/L.
